scores.one_line_rationale: Beautiful hero typography and a genuinely apt conceit - a gold meridian arc rising from '00 FIRST LIGHT' to '04 ZENITH' - but on the evidence it is one glowing arc over a starfield behind a scrim card rather than a system that organizes the page, the scrim visibly severs the arc, and nothing below the hero is visible anywhere in the captures.

notes: Biggest limitation: three builds (B3,B5,B6) render later acts into a pinned/fixed stage, so their whole-page captures are 66-85% flat empty colour and I can assess ONE act each - verified at native resolution that those bands are genuinely featureless, but cannot tell whether that means missing content or a scroll-driven stage a static fullpage screenshot cannot capture, so did not treat it as proof of emptiness. B1, B2 and B4 lay their acts out in normal flow and were easier to assess across the whole experience; THAT VISIBILITY DIFFERENCE MAY ADVANTAGE THEM ON CONTINUITY relative to how the pages actually behave. B5 is the one build where I could see state carried forward materially (sky lit differently in hero vs Noon viewport), which is why it scores 4 on continuity while B3 and B6, whose act structure I can only read from transport labels, do not. B1 vs B2 came out level on all four dimensions; ranked B1 above B2 purely on defect severity. Dimension 2 excluded as instructed. Everything about frame rate, easing quality, and whether input actually changes the render is unjudgeable here.
